rationale: Base rate (v2): Texas Democrats have won 0 of 13 Senate races since 1990 and Michigan Democrats about 9 of 10, so a joint base of 0.05. Strong evidence moves it up: October polls show Talarico leading Paxton by 2 to 4 points (TPOR +4, UH +2, Marist +2), though Texas polls have often overstated Democrats. El-Sayed leads Rogers by about 2 to 4 in the averages. Talarico is about a coin flip and El-Sayed is roughly 0.68; the two outcomes are correlated, giving about 0.36. A Michigan search result quoted market prices; I discarded it.

Base rate (v2): Democrats have won 8 of 8 Minnesota Senate races since 2006, so 0.9. Flanagan leads Tafoya by 3 to 5 in the averages (RCP +3.4, On Point +5.2), and Cook moved the race to Lean D, which points to some tightening. With a favorable national environment for Democrats, I shade the base down slightly to 0.83.

Base rate (v2): the ECB has hiked at roughly 10% of meetings since 1999 (about 220 meetings). Late-October previews from RSM, FXStreet, Nomura and Rabobank all expect a hold on October 29 and a possible hike in December. OIS pricing puts an October hike at about 3%. One result quoted a prediction-market figure; I discarded it.

Base rate (v2): an existing ceasefire surviving another three weeks is about 0.8, based on few cases. The ceasefire has held since spring, but escalation signals are strong. Trump says the US and Israel must 'finish the job', and reports say US strike options are ready for after the November 3 midterms. Netanyahu threatens a preemptive strike, and Iran promises a severe response. Talks are stalled, but Qatari mediation continues and much of the strike reporting relies on anonymous sources, so I land at 0.55.

Base rate (v2): Republicans have won 10 of 10 South Carolina Senate races since 2004, so 0.97. The race has become unusual: Lindsey Graham died, his appointed sister is the nominee, and she leads Andrews by only about 2 points in the averages. One Democratic internal poll shows Andrews ahead, and Cook moved the race to Lean R. Strong evidence of a close race in a strongly Republican state gives 0.78.

Base rate (v2): Democrats have won 1 of the last 9 Ohio governor races, so 0.12. Strong polling evidence moves it a long way: Acton leads Ramaswamy by about 3 to 4 in the averages (Marist +7, BGSU +6, Beacon +4), and Sabato moved the race to Lean D on October 22. Ohio polls have overstated Democrats in recent cycles, and only ActiVote has Ramaswamy ahead, so I hold at 0.55.

Base rate (v2): with Republicans holding 53 seats, a net loss of 4 or more seats in a midterm has happened about 4 times in 20, so Republicans keep control about 0.75 of the time. Strong evidence moves it down: Cook says a majority is 'squarely in Democrats' sights' and estimates 2 to 6 Democratic pickups. Non-market models give Democrats about 57 to 75% chance of control. Democrats lead or are close in Texas, Alaska and Kansas, giving about 0.33 for Republican control.

Base rate (v2): a general Russia-Ukraine ceasefire agreed in any given 5-day window is about 0.02. The only new deal is a local humanitarian truce in Oleshky, which the resolution excludes. Broader technical talks are not planned until November, and Russia still demands all of Donbas.

Base rate (v2): incumbent senators win re-election about 88% of the time, based on hundreds of cases. Peltola leads in most October polls, by about 1 to 3 points in the averages (NYT/Siena +7, Rasmussen Sullivan +1), and ranked-choice simulations are close. Alaska polls have historically understated Republicans badly (Sullivan led by about 5 in 2020 polls and won by 13), so I hold near even at 0.45. One result quoted market odds; I discarded it.

Base rate (v2): a specific named model releasing in a given 5-day window is about 0.1. Leaks say partners have Fable 5.5 access, an Azure/LiteLLM entry briefly appeared, and wccftech says it is 'tipped to land this week'. As of October 23, Anthropic's news page still listed Fable 5.1, a release predicted for the prior week did not happen, and the name itself is uncertain. My search budget ran out before I could check for any announcement after October 25.

YES means no US-Iran Hormuz agreement is announced by November 2. Base rate (v2): no deal in a given week of stalled talks is about 0.9. Talks have stalled for weeks, Trump rejected Iran's seven-day reopening offer, and the US is preparing post-midterm strike options. Only indirect messages are being passed, so a formal agreement accepted by both sides within a week is very unlikely.

Base rate (v2): a formal ceasefire in a 5-day window during active fighting is about 0.03. Saudi Arabia reportedly offered the Houthis $1B through Iran, and its defense minister visited Tehran. Riyadh officially rejects a new ceasefire, Houthi barrages continued on October 25, and both sides would need to announce acceptance. That gives a small upward adjustment to 0.06.
